newsitem.title: USA: Records set at Sotheby's sale in New York.
newsitem.headline: Records set at Sotheby's sale in New York.

text.p: An anonymous bidder paid nearly $12 million for Edgar Degas' sculpture "Petite Danseuse de Quatorze Ans" at Sotheby's on Tuesday night, a record for a Degas sculpture at auction.
The $11,882,500 bid was one of several record breakers on the opening night of Sotheby's Fall auction. The finest works brought exceptionally high prices, but the buyers were selective.
While all five pieces from the Shelburne Museum collection were aggressively bid on, 38 percent of the pieces offered were unsold by lot because they did not bring a minimum bid.
The Shelburne offered selections from its collection of Impressionist art based on a minimum guaranteed by Sotheby's, reported to be between $20 million and $23 million.

The works brought more than $28 million to the museum before Sotheby's auction fee was attached. Another anonymous bidder paid $8,692,500 for "Danseuse Jaune," a record for a Degas drawing at auction.

Another Degas drawing, "Danseuse a la Barre," brought $6,052,500, again from an anonymous bidder. Stephen Wynn, owner of the Mirage hotel in Las Vegas, bought "Portrait of Mademoiselle Suzette Lemaire," a drawing by Edouard Manet, for $2,917,500, a record price for a Manet at auction.
Wynn plans to display the work at his hotel. "This piece will go from Vermont to Las Vegas," said Sotheby's spokesperson Diana Brooks.

In the undersale, Paul Cezanne's "La Cote Du Galet, A Pontoise," topped the sales with a bid of $11,002,500. "Girls On A Bridge" by Edvard Munch brought $7,702,500, a record for the artist at auction.
Piet Mondrian's "Composition" went for $5,502,500. Claude Monet's "Nympheas" sold for $5,062,500.
